content.text: Coningsby’s summer at Beaumanoir introduces him to aristocratic manners, debates over the New Poor Law, and Eustace Lyle’s charitable paternalism at St. Genevieve. He travels to Manchester, studies its factories, and visits Millbank, where he meets Edith and encounters her father’s hostility toward the aristocracy. At Coningsby Castle he meets his grandfather, Sidonia, and Edith again, while political intrigue, social satire, performances, and a steeplechase unfold. Sidonia’s philosophy and Jewish identity profoundly influence him. Coningsby falls in love with Edith, but mistakenly believes she will marry Sidonia after witnessing their intimacy, and leaves Paris for England. Later, at Cambridge, he reunites with Oswald Millbank and Edith’s family, while mysteries surrounding his mother’s portrait and the feud between the families remain unresolved.
